# Executive Summary

R-LearnXR will provide open infrastructure for creating reproducible, browser-based virtual data laboratories with R and Quarto. R educators can readily publish code, text, and two-dimensional graphics, but an interactive multivariate lesson still requires authors to coordinate analysis data, browser rendering, learner prompts, accessible alternatives, environment locking, and publishing. Existing examples are often tied to one course or an opaque hosted service and are difficult for another instructor to adapt.

The project will turn a working prototype into a community-ready R package and lesson framework. Learners predict a result, edit and execute real R code locally through a pinned WebR runtime, inspect the returned data in a keyboard-operable 3D scene or semantic table, explain coordinate evidence, complete a transfer task, and export reproducible R or Quarto source. Authors will scaffold lessons, render scenes from R data frames, and run automated checks for deterministic seeds, environment locks, data licenses, accessible alternatives, and required learning-loop elements.

Grant work will stabilize the package API, add a third openly licensed example lesson, expand reproducibility and accessibility checks, conduct a small educator and learner pilot, and publish contributor training and maintenance documentation. The prototype reduces delivery risk by demonstrating the complete browser workflow now. We request **$10,000 for six months, January through June 2027**. Existing prototype development is in-kind evidence of feasibility and is not included as retroactive cost.
